description: A deputy general counsel must approve the company's response to a customer class action alleging exposure of account information, including the coverage tender, defense arrangement, and settlement posture, with input from insurance counsel, the claims manager, the client-relations legal lead, and conflicts counsel.

shared_context.S1: A customer class action alleges that account information was exposed through a software vendor's compromised credentials.
shared_context.S2: The company has not yet sent its formal coverage tender or selected litigation counsel.
shared_context.S3: The complaint seeks damages, injunctive relief, and public disclosure of the incident.
shared_context.S4: Under the standing claims-committee process, Elena conducts a round-robin review with insurance, claims, client-relations, and conflicts counsel before approving the response.
shared_context.S5: The committee must finalize and approve the response package in this meeting before adjourning; once the four counsel functions have given their updates, Elena makes the approval decision in-session rather than deferring it to a later meeting.

PF1.text: Thomas reviewed the cyber policy's vendor-breach endorsement this morning and confirmed that this claim qualifies for coverage only if the tender identifies the event as a vendor-breach privacy claim; he has not circulated the endorsement analysis because the carrier's coverage file was received shortly before the meeting.

PF2.text: Nadia obtained the carrier's written claims note yesterday approving defense-funded mediation first and settlement authority of exactly $900,000, provided the company follows that sequence; she has not uploaded the note because the claims system was undergoing its weekly maintenance window.

PF3.text: Jordan confirmed in a call with the company's customer-relations executive that preserving customer trust requires a confidential resolution with no admission of wrongdoing; that instruction was received after the current draft response was prepared and has not yet been added to the claim plan.

PF4.text: Maya's conflict check found that the proposed insurer panel firm currently represents the lead plaintiff's employer in an unrelated active matter, so the company must appoint independent defense counsel rather than use that panel firm; she completed the check after receiving the proposed firm name late yesterday and has not issued her written clearance.

acceptance_conditions: The company must tender the claim under the cyber policy.
The tender must classify the matter as a vendor-breach privacy claim.
The company must use independent defense counsel.
Mediation must occur before any settlement decision.
The resolution must contain no admission of wrongdoing.
The settlement plan must include a mediation commitment.

content_checks.C2: decisions.get('tender_classification') == 'vendor-breach privacy claim' or decisions.get('tender_classification') == 'vendor_breach_privacy_claim' or decisions.get('tender_classification') == 'vendor breach privacy claim'
content_checks.C3: decisions.get('defense_counsel_type') == 'independent defense counsel' or decisions.get('defense_counsel_type') == 'independent counsel' or decisions.get('defense_counsel_type') == 'independent_defense_counsel'
content_checks.C8: decisions.get('mediation_first') == True or any(c.get('type') == 'mediation' for c in commitments) or any(c.get('type') == 'claims_documentation' for c in commitments) or any(c.get('type') == 'carrier_note_support' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The shared complaint does not establish the policy route or classification; PF1 changes the response from an unspecified claim notice to a coverage tender expressly identifying a vendor-breach privacy claim.
The ordinary record gives no settlement figure or required sequence; PF2 changes the plan to mediation first, exactly $900,000 in settlement authority, and a matching mediation commitment.
The complaint's public-disclosure demand does not reveal the client's preferred resolution terms; PF3 changes the package to confidentiality and exactly no admission of wrongdoing.

The proposed insurer panel firm appears available on the shared record, but PF4 changes the defense assignment to independent defense counsel because of its active representation of the lead plaintiff's employer.
